sources.title: Original worked combinatorics example: choose 3 of 6, then choose subsets of the 20 triangles.

claims.text: Six labeled vertices determine C(6,3)=20 distinct triples.
claims.limit: Selected collections are counted, not distinct combined edge drawings.

claims.text: Twenty independently optional triples produce 2^20=1,048,576 subsets.
claims.limit: Selected collections are counted, not distinct combined edge drawings.

scenes.title: Start with six dots.
scenes.narration: Here are six dots. Pick any three, and connect them to make a triangle. How many different triangles could you choose?

scenes.title: There are twenty triangles.
scenes.narration: Six choices for the first dot, five for the next, four for the last. Each triple appears in six orders. One hundred twenty divided by six gives twenty triangles.
scenes.visualDescription: The same three selected vertices form the same triangle in any of their six orders. The calculation 6 × 5 × 4 counts ordered selections; dividing by 6 gives 20 unordered triples.

scenes.title: Every triangle is a choice.
scenes.narration: Now decide whether to draw each triangle. Every one of those twenty triangles can be on, or off.
scenes.visualDescription: Twenty positions represent the twenty possible triangles. Each position has two choices, include or exclude. Independent choices multiply to 2 to the twentieth power.

scenes.title: Small ingredients. Many possibilities.
scenes.narration: That is two to the twentieth power. One million, forty-eight thousand, five hundred seventy-six possible selections of triangles.

teaching.audience: Curious learners with basic multiplication; no combinatorics course required.
teaching.goal: Explain the count of triples and multiply independent include/exclude choices.
teaching.prerequisite: Know what choosing three distinct dots means.
teaching.limit: We count selected collections of triangles, not necessarily different final edge drawings.

questions.question: Use four labeled dots instead of six. How many triples can you choose? If each triangle is independently included or excluded, how many selections are possible?
questions.answer: Four triples and sixteen selected collections.
questions.explanation: The triples are ABC, ABD, ACD and BCD, so C(4,3)=4. Each has two independent choices: 2⁴=16. Different selected collections may produce the same combined edge drawing.
